subject: MAP: Benchmarking & Sizing — Acme Data HW evaluation (A100 / H100 / L40S, MIG vs full GPU)
body:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Fields <jordan@acmedata.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Benchmarking & Sizing — Acme Data HW evaluation (A100 / H100 / L40S, MIG vs full GPU)

Jordan — attaching the latest MAP and the summary from our perf run last week. Key asks below and proposed close timeline.

Summary (short):
- We ran three steady-state perf suites on your representative workload (30k prompt tokens/day baseline slices): A100 80GB, H100 80GB, L40S (full card) and representative MIG splits on A100/H100.
- Measured metrics: p50/p95 latency (single request, 512 token generation), TTFT for streaming-first-token, sustained throughput (tokens/sec) at 95% SLO, and concurrency curves up to 128 concurrent streams.
- Results and sizing recommendation are in the attached PDF and MAP sheet. High level: H100 gives ~1.5x throughput vs A100 at same batch and ~25% lower p95 for our decoding profiles; L40S is cost-effective for lower-concurrency, but has lower KV cache capacity impacting long-context workloads. MIG provides good density for many small concurrent sessions, but with noticeable TTFT penalty for cold-starts on our model variants.

Open items for MAP:
- Confirm target concurrency profile (Jordan: you mentioned 40-60 active sessions during peak).
- Procurement lead time: Acme to confirm if they prefer monthly dedicated or annual Reserved.
- Compliance: we validated KMS interplay in Private — CS needs one more audit doc.

Proposed near-term timeline:
- 10/05: finalize MAP (action items + roles) — owner: Jordan / Monica
- 10/09: agree on target SKU mix for pilot (H100-heavy vs mixed) — owner: Karthik / Jordan
- 10/20: pilot end + decision meeting (close target) — owner: Monica / Acme execs

Attachments: MAP_Acme_v3.xlsx (MAP with milestones), benchmark-summary-A100-H100-L40S.pdf (summary + graphs), ttft-concurrency-raw.csv (raw results)

Thanks — LMK if you'd like a quick 20-min walk-through of the PDF.

— Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP_Acme_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 52KB)]

From: Jordan Fields <jordan@acmedata.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Benchmarking & Sizing — Acme Data HW evaluation (A100 / H100 / L40S, MIG vs full GPU)

Thanks Monica — this looks helpful. Quick answers:
- Concurrency target: 50 peak active sessions, with planned burst capacity up to 90 for seasonal loads.
- Preference: we want predictable p95 under 300ms for short completions (<=128 tokens) and TTFT < 200ms for chat-first-token.
- Procurement: procurement@acmedata.com will own purchasing; prefer annual reserved if cost delta is reasonable.

Can Karthik and team recommend an SKU mix that keeps p95 under target with minimum cost? Also please confirm whether MIG will consistently meet our TTFT goal or if it only works for sustained throughput.

— Jordan

----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jordan Fields <jordan@acmedata.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Benchmarking & Sizing — SKU mix proposal

Jordan / team — I pulled the perf runs into a cost/latency synthesis and sketched three SKU mixes in the MAP sheet:
Option A (performance-first): 70% H100 full GPUs, 30% H100 MIG for density. Expected p95 180-220ms, TTFT median ~150ms, supports 60 sustained concurrency with headroom. Higher cost but simplest for long-context tasks.
Option B (balanced): 40% H100 full, 40% A100 full, 20% L40S. Expected p95 240-320ms on mixed workloads; TTFT median ~180-230ms. Best cost-performance balance for bursty chat use.
Option C (density): 20% full H100, 60% H100/A100 MIG slices, 20% L40S. Lower unit cost, higher TTFT cold starts (median TTFT 250-400ms) — recommended only if Acme is willing to accept slightly higher first-token latency for up to 2x cost reduction.

Notes on MIG: we observed a consistent TTFT penalty of ~40-120ms on cold sessions depending on slice size and model KV footprint; however, at high-concurrency the tokens/sec per dollar is superior. For long-run sustained throughput H100 full gives best tail latency.

Action requested: Jordan, confirm whether priority is hard p95 / TTFT targets or cost reduction. If p95 is critical, we recommend Option A for the pilot.

— Karthik

----
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jordan Fields <jordan@acmedata.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmarking results — detailed numbers

Attaching summarized graphs inline and called out numbers below (see full PDF for plots):
- A100 80GB (baseline): p50=38ms, p95=420ms (512 tokens, greedy decoding, single stream), TTFT median=220ms, sustained throughput ~1.0x
- H100 80GB (optimized kernels): p50=28ms, p95=290ms, TTFT median=160ms, sustained throughput ~1.5x vs A100
- L40S (40GB class): p50=48ms, p95=510ms, TTFT median=240ms; good throughput per $ for short sessions but cache pressure for long contexts.
- MIG 7g (H100): p95 tail varies by slice; p95 ~320-500ms depending on co-tenancy; TTFT cold-start penalty +60-120ms.

Concurrency curves: H100 full holds p95 < 300ms up to ~70 concurrent streams for our model; A100 full crosses 300ms p95 near 50 concurrent streams. MIG mixes sustain tokens/sec but p95 degrades sooner if co-tenancy is not isolated.

Testbed notes: model quantized to 4-bit, same prompt sets as MAP doc, synthetic traffic with stochastic session starts to emulate your user behavior. All raw logs in ttft-concurrency-raw.csv.

Recommendations (concise):
- Pilot: H100-heavy pool for latency-sensitive endpoints (chat-first-token and short completions).
- Scale: introduce MIG for low-cost batch/background tasks or when per-session memory <= 20GB.
- Cache strategy: enable prefix/KV caching for long-context workflows to reduce p95 impact on L40S.

— Soojin (Perf Eng)

[Attachment: benchmark-summary-A100-H100-L40S.pdf (report, 1.2MB)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Fields <jordan@acmedata.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final MAP recommendation for pilot

Jordan / Monica — based on the stated p95/TTFT targets and the perf data, my recommended pilot config is:
- 8 x H100 full GPUs (serving pool for latency-sensitive chat endpoints)
- 4 x L40S for cost-effective non-interactive tasks (embeddings, bulk rerank)
- Optionally 12 MIG slices (H100 7g) pre-warmed for scheduled batch jobs and low-memory sessions

Estimated monthly cost (region us-west): Reserved annual commit gives ~18% discount vs on-demand. We included cost sims in the MAP sheet. This configuration should meet p95 < 300ms at 50 concurrent sessions and supply headroom for bursts to 90.

Next steps:
- Jordan: confirm pilot SKU mix by 10/20 meeting (requested)
- Monica / Laura: align procurement and CS audit docs (Laura to send SOC2 sub-item)

— Rishi (Solutions Architect)
